roll.name: The six traditions’ own chronologies (the lanes panel)
roll.used_for: the lanes under the map: what six reckonings claim, beside the dated record
roll.source: RESEARCH_Synchronoptic_Lanes_Sourcing.md Part A (54 sources), tracked in this repo at docs/RESEARCH_Synchronoptic_Lanes_Sourcing.md. Per-item sources are on the items.
roll.licence: The dates are facts and claims reported from the cited scholarship and are not themselves copyrightable; the wording here is this project’s.
roll.data: data/lanes/lanes.json — 17 lanes, 66 items, 10 alignments, 3 gap connectors, generated by geowork/lanes/build_lanes.py. Per-item sources are on the items.
roll.changes: Changes were made, and two are editorial rather than mechanical. Where a tradition gives a LENGTH but no DATE, this map chose the anchor its mythic era hangs on: the Sumerian King List’s flood on the Shuruppak deposit, drawn as a RANGE at c. 3000-2900 BCE because that is the precision the evidence has, and Manetho’s divine reigns on Dynasty 1 at 3111-3045 BCE. Both are drawn as approximate and both say in their own tooltip that the placement is ours and not the text’s. The Kali Yuga epoch is NOT marked approximate, because 3102 BCE is the tradition’s own computed date. Mechanically: dates converted to years-ago against the map’s axis, coincident claims clustered and separated again in the tooltip, and the region lanes derived by placing each anchor in the boxes data/borders/coverage.json defines.
roll.note: Every lane item carries the source it came from, because a reader is entitled to know which tradition, and which scholar, a line on this chart is reporting.
